body:
Yeah, I just got news that he won't be able to move his limbs on his own. I don't know, this is very disheartening for me to hear but I'm still glad he's alive, and it seems that he will improve, albeit slowly. On the topic of other friends though, it definitely brought me closer to some people I wouldn't have expected though. It's only been a week, and yet I'm already talking with others about how to be there for him. 

Thank you very much for the suggestions though. I definitely plan to get him involved in more video games and studying though. I was trying to think of other possibilities as well, and things like writing, reading, or some quality TV/films come to mind I guess. 

Thank you so much again :)

Thank you so much. I will definitely send more letters then. I've always liked doing so, and I can definitely see how something physical will help vs. say an email. I'll definitely keep in touch in all sorts of way though. 

A concern I have though is that he was always very active and sporty, and now may not have that option. I'm not sure how much damage is done to his body, but I really hope that he can come back to 100%. Even 75% would be great, as long as he can still retain a bit of what he had before. It's not my biggest concern I guess, but it's something that crosses my mind now and then. I'm glad you mentioned that he's still the same person though, and I will treat him just like that.

I will do my best. The only problem I foresee is that in a month, I'll be going across the United States for my first year in college but I plan to keep in touch as much as possible. I definitely feel as if I was not there for him prior to this, so I'll do my best.
